key_insight: An AI-accelerated bottom-up polymerization model predicts the amorphous microstructure and diffraction signatures of poly(1,3-dioxolane) across chain growth, revealing distinct monomer and polymer contributions to the main scattering peak.
engineering_relevance: This enables atomistic structure prediction for UHMW recyclable polymers where diffraction alone cannot resolve amorphous condensed-phase microstructure, supporting design and validation of process-structure-property relationships.
method: Simulated living cationic ring-opening polymerization under experimental conditions using the AI²-BPSP framework.
Used machine-learning force fields trained to van der Waals-corrected hybrid DFT data.
Partitioned X-ray and neutron diffraction signals into monomer and growing-chain contributions to track chain-length evolution.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports statistically significant, first-principles, chain-length-resolved diffraction predictions with a monomer peak near q≈1.5 Å⁻¹ that decays and a polymer peak near q≈1.6 Å⁻¹ that grows and is absent in oligomers.
watch_item: Predictions still need direct experimental validation, and the accuracy depends on transferability of the trained force field and the assumed synthetic conditions.
paper_title: Bottom-Up Prediction of Amorphous Poly(1,3-dioxolane) using Ab Initio Reactive Machine-Learning Force Fields
